- **#485 closed (2026-10-20), with its post-deployment review** (programme
  #64, three review rounds, the third finding nothing material). Its first
  lesson, that a post-deployment check covers each clause of its requirement,
  is now in 1.2 and the raise-project skill. The second is left here as a
  lesson rather than a rule: whoever merges a workflow that needs a secret
  runs it by hand that day and confirms it did its work, because the board
  sweep's first run passed green with no token. The owner also set out the
  phases: deployed moves to `Post-deployment`, checks passed to
  `Project Closedown`, and lessons documented and actioned closes it.
  Actioning means putting each finding on a project or requirement issue, or
  in the next weekly digest; a project does not stay open to implement
  follow-on changes. *Proposed conclusion:* consider writing the phase
  meanings into 1.2, which does not yet mention the weekly digest as a home
  for a finding.
  - *Conclusion:* Agreed with the owner, 2026-10-27: the phase meanings are programme #68, awaiting the owner's review, so no further action. The secret-workflow lesson: monitor `P-3`, a new occurrence (the sweep passed green with no token).
- **delphside/tile-lite-elite#520, the Ticket lifecycle, passed its live
  test (2026-10-20).** Three lessons. The Ticket Kind field was believed to
  exist since #516 and did not; a field a package depends on is checked by
  listing it, not from memory. The shared board token needed the
  organisation's *issue fields* permission as well as Projects, or GraphQL
  answers FORBIDDEN; the service-desk README names it. The organisation
  issue-field lookup has to name the concrete field types, because the common
  interface fails. *Proposed conclusion:* monitor; the token's permissions are
  recorded where it is set up.
  - *Conclusion:* Agreed with the owner, 2026-10-27: monitor `P-5`, a new occurrence (a field believed to exist was never checked). The token's permissions are recorded in the service-desk README: no further action.
- **delphside/tile-lite-elite#515, the support desk, closed (2026-10-22)**
  after #518 shipped in Tile Lite Elite 0.10.0 and every check passed. On
  production a support email became a Ticket in 21 seconds, game emails carry
  the support Reply-To, and the acknowledgement and a `reply` both reached the
  sender. Two lessons from the release. First, the version gate refused 0.9.2
  because #518 is functional, a rule (docs/4.3.3 §2.4.2) that the overnight
  regression brief did not check, so preview and rehearsal had to be run again
  for 0.10.0. Second, the rename of `programme.toml` left the old name in the
  profile's `non_shipping` list, so deploys warned falsely about #527 (fixed by
  TLE #540). *Proposed conclusion:* a release brief reads the milestone's
  `Type of change` before rehearsal. Whoever renames a file the profile names
  searches the profile for the old name. The owner's point (2026-10-22): the
  review should have caught it, and checks will never cover every mistake, so
  the question for this review is where review stops and an automatic check
  starts. #540 added a test for this one case.
  - *Conclusion:* Agreed with the owner, 2026-10-27: the release brief reads the milestone's `Type of change` before rehearsal, a fix to Tile Lite Elite's docs/4.3.3. The rename: monitor `P-2`, a new occurrence (a name in two places drifted). Review catches a mistake the first time, and one with a `P-` row is a candidate for an automatic check: process changed, in 1.4's problem register. #540's test for the profile name is early, but cheap, and stays.
- 2026-10-26, this digest: `board-digest.py` cannot run from a cloud thread.
